items.headline: Dollar extends to a fresh 19-month high into the NY close — DXY ~103.34 (+0.2%); EUR/USD ~$1.1036, lowest since April 2025; USD/JPY ~159.93 after touching 160.19 in Tokyo; best dollar week in two months (Reuters).

PPI core read corrected: the standard core (ex-food-and-energy) printed +0.3% m/m, +5.0% y/y — exactly in line; the +0.5% was the trade-inclusive core (less foods, energy, trade). Post-print FedWatch 25bp 88.2% / 50bp 11.8% (CME).
Daly: 'rate increases likely' as inflation worsens — bias is further tightening, inflation 'bleeding' into services; rising yields 'most welcome', giving the Fed 'a little more time' (Reuters).
Bowman: core PCE seen at 3.3% in Oct; wants the AI and Middle East shocks to dissipate before believing inflation falls next year (FXStreet).
Collins: higher productivity has helped limit some inflation pressures; Logan: Treasury market functions 'very well' (squawk).
BofA adds a January 2027 hike to its Fed forecast and a third hike by March 2027; STIR ~28bp priced for December (squawk).

Oil flat into the close — Brent ~$96.12, WTI ~$88.93 — after the IEA surplus call; Brent -2.5% on the week. CENTCOM denies the IRGC radar-hit claim, says it shot down two IRGC drones headed for Bahrain; Iran says an LNG tanker hit a mine in Hormuz (Reuters).
CFTC Nov 10 COT due 2:30pm CT — not yet posted on the CFTC site at push time; the Nov 3 cut (released Nov 6) is still the latest scored.
IEA: global oil market returns to surplus in Q4 for the first time since the Iran war — supply 105 mb/d, 1.7 mb/d above demand; Brent ~$95.7, WTI ~$88.4 after Thu's +$3.06 settle jump (IEA; Reuters).
Eurozone Q3 GDP 2nd estimate +0.4% q/q, unrevised from the Oct 30 flash; +1.3% y/y; employment flat — no EUR reaction, EUR/USD ~$1.1065 (Eurostat; Reuters).
2Y Treasury +34bp over two sessions, the sharpest two-day rise in 3.5 years — 2Y ~4.86%, 10Y ~5.11% — as the December hike reprices (Reuters).

Williams (NY Fed) Thursday panel: the Fed 'still has work to do' to get policy to the right place — 'the economy is strong, labor market continues to strengthen, and inflation is persistent' (Morningstar/DJ).
Oil settles +$3.06 — Brent $95.82, WTI $88.74 — as Houthis claim attacks on Saudi energy sites (East-West pipeline, Yanbu, Aramco Riyadh) and four tankers are hit in Hormuz (Reuters).
USD/JPY touches 160.04 Thursday, closes 159.83 — FinMin Katayama Friday: government will 'respond appropriately' to FX volatility; Dec BoJ hike ~84% intact (Reuters).
Dollar holds the 19-month high in Asia — DXY ~103.15, flat after the three-day CPI rally; EUR/USD ~$1.1055, GBP/USD ~$1.3237, USD/JPY ~159.88 (Reuters Asia wrap).
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns — NVDA -5.8% at midday, AMD +5.6% on an upgrade; S&P +0.2%, Nasdaq flat as the AI trade absorbs the leadership shock (Motley Fool).
Existing-home sales -5.5% to 3.75M SAAR in Oct, lowest since Aug 2010 (vs 3.85M fcst); 30Y mortgage averaged 7.33% in Oct, peaking near 7.40% (NAR; Reuters).

Oct Treasury deficit $404B, a record for the month and +42% y/y (receipts $369B, outlays a record $773B); FY2026 deficit $1.992T, 6.2% of GDP; the $25B 30Y auction tailed 0.4bp (5.441%, BTC 2.36) (Treasury; Reuters; ZeroHedge).

Goolsbee: inflation 'well-above target', 'sober minded' on pace — 25bp and keep going; Dec 25bp ~91% (CME FedWatch), 50bp tail ~9-12%; 87bp of hikes priced over the year ahead; Williams panel this evening (InvestingLive; Barchart).

Claims MISS — initial jobless claims 200,000 (vs 194K fcst), up 9,000 from a revised 191,000; 4-wk avg 195,250 flat; continuing claims 1,697,000 (-20,000). Dollar steady ~103.0 after the print — the 6K miss sits below the ~210K level where Dec hike bets would trim (DOL).
items.source: DOL: Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims — https://www.dol.gov/ui/data.pdf

items.headline: UK Q3 GDP +0.7% q/q in line (fastest pace in 2.5 years; y/y 1.9%) — but Q2 revised to a -1.0% contraction (from +0.5%); Sep +0.2% m/m beat (fcst 0.0%); IP Sep +0.3% m/m beat. GBP/USD ~$1.3271 steady; Dec BoE back-to-back ~75% (Reuters).
items.source: Reuters Nov 12 — https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/sterling-steady-after-uk-gdp-data-fed-official-up-next-2026-11-12/ ; ONS GDP monthly estimate

items.headline: Abu Dhabi three-way talks: Russia-Ukraine-US agree a major prisoner exchange but territorial issues unresolved; US envoys head to Moscow; Russia struck Ukraine's power grid overnight even as talks opened; Lavrov: no immediate ceasefire.

BoJ dove Asada pushes back on the pace of hikes — premature moves could cool growth and push down underlying inflation; consumption 'lacking momentum'; neutral rate on the lower side of the 1.1–2.5% staff range. Dec hike ~84% intact; USD/JPY ~159.65–159.83, MoF warns on rapid moves (Reuters/FXStreet, Nov 12).
Japan PPI beats +7.1% y/y (fcst 6.5%, Sep +6.8%); +0.7% m/m; yen-based import prices +24.8% y/y — Dec BoJ hike case firms (BoJ official via Reuters, Nov 12).
